court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Shirish Suryakant Pathak And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Shirish Suryakant Pathak and others (original accused)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra and another

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Original accused seeking quashing of FIR and criminal proceedings for offences under IPC, Dowry Prohibition Act. Parties have arrived at an amicable settlement.

legal_principles.principle: The power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences.
legal_principles.held: Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
Madhu Limaye v. State of Maharashtra (1977) 4 SCC 551
State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent abuse of the process of any Court

legal_principles.principle: Heinous and serious offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.
legal_principles.held: Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent harm to society

outcome.final_order: Quashing of FIR and criminal proceedings ordered on settlement terms.
